  "text": "The library rang to say a photograph had been found in a returned book.

“There's a name on the back,” the woman said. “Yours, I think.”

Helen went after lunch. Rain had collected in the grooves of the library steps.

The woman at the desk handed her a small envelope.

“We keep them for a month. After that, we're never sure what to do.”

The photograph showed Helen's father beside a half-built wall. He held a trowel in one hand and a sandwich in the other. Behind him, washing hung across a garden Helen didn't recognise.

“Is it yours?”

“Yes. I lent it to my sister.”

Outside, Helen stood under the awning and called her.

“Which book?” her sister asked.

“I didn't ask.”

“Something about gardens, probably. I was going to show you that wall.”

“What about it?”

“He built it at our first house. Before you were born.”

Helen looked again at the washing. A striped sheet bellied towards the camera.

“I thought he hated doing things like that.”

“He hated finishing them.”

A bus passed, pushing water towards the kerb.

“Have you eaten?” her sister asked.

“Not yet.”

“There's soup.”

Helen put the photograph back in its envelope and crossed when the lights changed.

Her sister lived fifteen minutes away. At the gate, Helen noticed a loose brick on the low wall. She pressed it with her palm, then left it alone.

The door opened before she knocked.

“Let me see,” her sister said.

They carried the photograph into the kitchen, where two bowls were already on the table."
